svg.text: Steering noise and grip variation applied separately, then together. Applying only the combination would have shown fragility without saying what the car was actually sensitive to.
steering noise, attentive driver, sigma = 0.01 (1.6 deg at the wheel)
both together, distracted driver, sigma = 0.03 (4.7 deg at the wheel)
the ORIGINAL noise level (F96) — 23 deg at the wheel, not a driver; kept only so the correction is visible in the data
both, harder still — most laps leave the fit; direction only
Ranges are 95% Wilson intervals at n = 40 rollouts per cell. Where two intervals overlap, the two cells are not distinguishable and no ranking between them is claimed.
The nominal row is Episode 10's measurement, repeated here so the perturbed rows have something from the same code path to be compared against.

[MEASURED] Episode 10's policy (experiments/ep10/out/policy.pt), DEPLOYED, nothing retrained - 120 rollouts per design (headline rates); 40 for the condition grid - [ASSUMED] steering noise sigma 0.01, grip +/-20% per lap - slip envelope penalised at 0.5
Finish rate is the DEPLOYED policy's — mean action, no exploration noise. The steering noise here is a disturbance the deployed car actually experiences, which is a different thing entirely.
